cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Make It Their Idea
cards.instruction: Make an unwanted task sound appealing enough that someone volunteers for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I may permit you to reorganize our shed. Your tools deserve better surroundings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I throw out your paint tins?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Disposal is approved. A designer of your calibre shouldn't have to work around clutter.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And can I give myself a shelf you can't touch?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That shelf will have my protection, even from me. Would you like to choose where it goes? We could start with the clutter around it.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 permission to reorganize, A3 approved disposal and A5 protected shelf make A's superior grants the reason B might choose the task.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 paint-tin request gets A3 disposal approval; B4 excluding A gets A5 self-binding protection and a placement invitation.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 ask for practical autonomy, making willingness to tackle clutter contingent on meaningful control.

heightening.evidence: B4 tests whether freedom includes protection from A; A5 grants that limit from above while inviting the first clearing choice.

specificity.evidence: A1 shed and tools, B2 paint tins and B4 shelf specify the unwanted job and its reward.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 protection even from me earns its rank-preserving concession from B4 a shelf A cannot touch.
